issue: The figure note says each column is a separate completion 'after 4 turns', but the x-axis columns are turns 0–4; only the last column is after four turns. This contradicts the plotted x-axis and the caption's per-turn formula.
evidence: Figure note: 'counterfactual: each column = a separate completion after 4 turns including one final 300-token answer'. X-axis labels: '0 (single-shot)', '1', '2', '3', '4'. Caption: 'each column is a counterfactual completion (9,200 input + 300 output + 800 + 65 per turn)'. If every column were after 4 turns, all bars would be 12,960 tokens / 34.0 GB, not the plotted 9,500→12,960 tokens and 24.9→34.0 GB.
acceptance_test: Revise the note to 'each column = a separate completion after the indicated number of turns (0–4)' and verify every column's token/KV value matches I0 + T·δ + T·γ + O_final at its own T.

issue: The orange annotation 'generated γ=65/turn' is placed over the bar fills rather than in clear white space, reducing legibility at print size; the orange text/arrow also has weak grayscale contrast against the blue hatched and green dotted fills.
evidence: Panel (a): the annotation text and arrow overlap the turn-2/turn-3 bars around the 8,000-token level. The generated segment itself is only 65 tokens per turn, so the arrow points to a very thin sliver. At 150 dpi the text is readable on screen, but at print size the orange-on-hatch contrast is marginal.
acceptance_test: Move the annotation to white space or add an opaque white background; verify at print size that the text and arrow are legible in both color and grayscale, and that the arrow clearly terminates on the orange segment.

issue: The figure's explanatory annotations below each bar are set in very small type and are crowded against the bar labels and x-axis, making them hard to read at print size.
evidence: Annotations such as '[DERIVED] bounding case — nothing evicted; bounds what the system tolerates' and '[ILLUSTRATIVE] evicts the reusable prefix — moves cache memory and re-prefill' are rendered in a small font beneath the bars. The x-axis label and the counterfactual note are also small and tightly stacked. At 150 dpi they are legible on screen, but at 8.5×11 print size the annotation block is borderline.
acceptance_test: Increase the annotation type size or move the annotations into the caption/figure note; verify at print size that all annotation text is comfortably readable without magnification.

issue: The table's colored row labels and colored arrows rely on color to distinguish models and directions; in grayscale the red, blue, and green labels/arrows collapse to similar gray values, although the row text and numeric values remain readable.
evidence: Rows are colored red ('DeepSeek V4-Flash'), blue ('DeepSeek V4-Pro'), and green ('GLM-5.3-Flash'); the '100% → ~7%' arrows are also colored. In grayscale the colored text and arrows lose their hue distinction. The table still has row labels and numbers, so the information is not lost, but the color encoding is not grayscale-safe.
acceptance_test: Add a non-color differentiator (e.g., row-label prefixes, distinct arrow styles, or direct labels) and verify the table remains unambiguous in grayscale.
